mainTopic: Lighting one חנוכה lamp from another (מנר לנר), and the איבעיא of whether הדלקה or הנחה fulfills the מצוה
overview: This amud continues the מחלוקת between רב, who forbids lighting one חנוכה lamp from another (מנר לנר), and שמואל, who permits it. First, a ברייתא about מעשר שני seems to refute שמואל: holy money may not be used as a weight, even to redeem other מעשר שני. רבה answers that this ban is a special גזירה that applies only to weighing. Next, רב ששת challenges רב from the מנורה in the מקדש, where the other lamps were lit from the miraculous נר מערבי. That practice seems to contradict both reasons given for רב: בזוי מצוה and אכחושי מצוה. רב פפא answers that long wicks were used, which saves the בזוי מצוה reason, but the אכחושי מצוה reason remains a קשיא. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע then rules that the law depends on whether the lighting (הדלקה) or the placing (הנחה) is the act that fulfills the מצוה. The גמרא brings this question as an איבעיא. It pushes off two proofs from רבא, since in both cases an onlooker would think the lamp was for personal use. The amud ends as the גמרא starts a third proof from רבי יהושע בן לוי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא about weighing gold against מעשר שני money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא: you may not weigh gold dinars against מעשר שני coins, even if your goal is to redeem other מעשר שני with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Coins of] מעשר שני: one may not weigh gold dinars against them, and this applies even if he wants to redeem other מעשר שני produce with [the gold].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that it brought as a challenge against שמואל. It says that holy מעשר שני money may not be used as a counterweight, even for another holy purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key point is the word 'even' (ואפילו). Using a holy object for a private benefit is forbidden even when the goal is another holy purpose, such as redeeming more מעשר שני. This looks similar to using one חנוכה lamp to light another, which is why it is a problem for שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: The second tithe, holy produce or money that must be eaten or spent in ירושלים
Weighing against it, using it as a counterweight
To redeem, to transfer holiness from produce onto money

phrases.english: [Coins of] second tithe: one may not weigh against them
phrases.notes: The start of this ברייתא appeared on the previous amud.

phrases.english: gold dinars,
and even in order to redeem upon it
phrases.notes: 'Even' is the key word: a holy goal does not make it permitted.

phrases.english: other second-tithe [produce].

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְחַלֵּל עָלָיו מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that was brought against שמואל earlier.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל, who permits lighting from lamp to lamp
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a holy item may not be used even for another holy purpose, then a חנוכה lamp should not be used to light another חנוכה lamp.

steps.title: Whether the ברייתא refutes שמואל depends on the wood chip
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains when the ברייתא is a refutation. If שמואל forbids lighting with a wood chip, there is no problem. If he permits even that, the ברייתא refutes him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is fine if you say that רב and שמואל only argue about lighting directly from lamp to lamp, and with a wood chip שמואל forbids it. Then [the ברייתא] is not a refutation. But if you say that he permits it even with a wood chip, then it is a refutation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly how far the ברייתא's challenge reaches. It only hurts שמואל if he permits lighting even with a wood chip (קינסא).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lighting directly from lamp to lamp uses the lamp itself for the מצוה, so it is not like the weighing case. Lighting with a wood chip brings in an outside object for a non-מצוה step, which is closer to using מעשר שני money as a weight. So the refutation only works if שמואל allows the wood chip too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine / granted (sets up a contrast with a version that has a problem)
A wood chip or splinter used to carry a flame
From one lamp to another lamp

phrases.english: It is fine if you say

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פְּלִיגִי רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל מִנֵּר לְנֵר
phrases.english: that when Rav and Shmuel disagree, it is about [lighting directly] from lamp to lamp
but with a wood chip, Shmuel forbids —
then this will not be a refutation.
But if you say
that he permits even with a wood chip —
then this would be a refutation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains exactly when the ברייתא from step 1 counts as a refutation of שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל, if he permits lighting even with a קינסא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids using a holy item even for another holy purpose. That matches using a lit lamp and a wood chip to light another lamp.

steps.title: רבה: the weighing case has its own special concern
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that weighing מעשר שני money was forbidden for a separate reason. The weights may not match, and then the person may end up using the money for a mundane purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is a rabbinic decree, in case his weights do not come out exactly equal, and then he takes them out for a mundane (חולין) purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends שמואל. He says the ברייתא is not a general rule about using holy items for holy purposes. It is a special גזירה that only fits the weighing case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When weighing, the person might find the gold does not match. He might then decide not to redeem at all, so the מעשר שני coins would have been used for a plain, non-holy weighing. Lighting a חנוכה lamp, even with a wood chip, is clearly done for the מצוה, so this worry does not apply there.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
It is a decree, in case he does not get his weights exactly equal
and he will take them out for a mundane [purpose].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא לֹא יְכַוֵּין מִשְׁקְלוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in steps 1–2 by showing that the ברייתא's reason is unique to weighing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the ברייתא's ban comes from a special גזירה, not from a general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא teaches that holy items may never be used, even for another holy purpose, so שמואל would be refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban is only a decree about uneven weights leading to mundane use. It does not apply to lighting חנוכה lamps, so שמואל stands.

steps.title: רב ששת opens a challenge from the מנורה in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת quotes a ברייתא: the מנורה was not needed for light, since ישראל walked by הקב״ה's light in the desert. Rather, it was a testimony that the שכינה rests among ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת raised an objection: 'Outside the curtain of the testimony he shall arrange it.' Does [הקב״ה] need its light? All forty years that בני ישראל walked in the desert, didn't they walk only by His light? Rather, it is a testimony to all mankind that the שכינה rests among ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת starts a new challenge against רב's view. This step sets up the background, that the מנורה was a 'testimony.' The actual challenge comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the word עדות ('testimony') in the פסוק as describing the purpose of the מנורה, since הקב״ה obviously does not need light. This leads to the question of what exactly the testimony was, and that answer will become the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection (usually from a ברייתא)
The curtain in front of the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raised an objection:
"Outside the curtain of the testimony he shall arrange [it]" (ויקרא כד:ג),
Does He need its light?
Isn't it so that all forty years
that the Children of Israel walked in the desert
they walked only by His light!
phrases.notes: Referring to the pillar of fire.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a testimony to all mankind
that the Divine Presence rests among Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the מעשר שני challenge is answered, a new challenge begins, this time against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that one may not light from lamp to lamp
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This sets up a source about the מקדש מנורה. In the following steps it will show lamp-to-lamp lighting was done there.

steps.title: What was the testimony?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the 'testimony' of the מנורה was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question about the ברייתא it just quoted. It sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step said the מנורה was a testimony but did not say how anyone could see it. This question asks for the visible sign that showed the שכינה was present.

phrases.english: What is the testimony?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the 'testimony' mentioned in step 4 actually was.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What visible sign made the מנורה a testimony to the שכינה

steps.title: רב: the miracle of the נר מערבי
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the testimony was the נר מערבי. It received the same amount of oil as the other lamps, yet it kept burning. The כהן lit the others from it and ended with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: This is the western lamp, which received the same amount of oil as the others. From it he would light [the others], and with it he would finish.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. The miracle of the נר מערבי, which burned longer than it naturally should, was the testimony. Notice the detail that the other lamps were lit from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'from it he would light' (וממנה היה מדליק) are the part רב ששת needs. They show that in the מקדש a lamp of מצוה was used to light other lamps of מצוה. That seems to go against רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The western lamp of the מנורה
The same measure as its fellow lamps

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two רבs here. רב (the אמורא who explains the testimony) is the same רב whose ruling on חנוכה is being challenged. רב ששת is a different אמורא, the one raising the challenge.

phrases.english: Rav said:
This is the western lamp
in which he puts oil in the same measure as its fellow [lamps],
and from it he would light [the others]
phrases.notes: This is the key detail for רב ששת's challenge.

phrases.english: and with it he would finish.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The testimony was the miraculous נר מערבי, from which the other lamps were lit.

steps.title: The fixed lamps required lighting with a wood chip
steps.stepSummary: Since the מנורה's lamps were fixed in place, the כהן had to take a flame (with a wood chip) from the נר מערבי to light the others. That contradicts both possible reasons for רב's ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, since the lamps were fixed in place, there was no choice except to take [a flame on a chip] and light. This is difficult both for the one who says [the reason is] disrespect to the מצוה and for the one who says [the reason is] weakening the מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: Now רב ששת makes his actual challenge. In the מקדש, lamp-to-lamp lighting with a wood chip was done, which goes against רב's ban under either explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a wood chip contradicts the בזוי מצוה reason, which objects to lighting with a chip. Lighting one מצוה lamp from another contradicts the אכחושי מצוה reason, which objects to seeming to 'weaken' the first lamp. So the מקדש practice is a problem for both reasons.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no way other than

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next steps. One answer can remove the problem for one reason but not the other, which shows how the two reasons really differ.

phrases.english: But here, since the lamps were fixed in place,
there is no choice but to take [a wood chip] and light.
It is difficult both for the one who says
[the reason is] because of disrespect to the מצוה,
and for the one who says
[the reason is] because of weakening the מצוה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the detail 'ממנה היה מדליק' from step 6 against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both explanations of רב's ban (בזוי מצוה and אכחושי מצוה)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the מקדש they used a wood chip, against בזוי מצוה, and lit lamp from lamp, against אכחושי מצוה.

steps.title: רב פפא: the wicks were long
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the מנורה had long wicks, so the כהן could light directly from one lamp to the next without a wood chip.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא explained it as referring to long wicks.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers part of רב ששת's challenge. Long wicks could be pulled from one lamp to reach the next, so no wood chip was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a wood chip, there is no disrespect, so the בזוי מצוה reason is no longer contradicted. But lamp-to-lamp lighting still happened, so this answer does not help the אכחושי מצוה reason.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa explained it
as referring to long wicks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers part of the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: no wood chip was used
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fixed lamps forced the use of a wood chip.
steps.terutzMaskana: Long wicks allowed direct lighting, so the בזוי מצוה reason is safe.

steps.title: The weakening reason is still contradicted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that even with long wicks, a lamp was still lit from a lamp. So the אכחושי מצוה reason is still contradicted.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, for the one who says [the reason is] weakening the מצוה, it is still difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב פפא's answer only solves half the problem. The 'weakening' explanation still has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אכחושי מצוה concern is about lighting from one lamp to another at all, whatever tool is used. The long-wick answer removes the wood chip but not the lamp-to-lamp lighting, so this side of the challenge remains.

phrases.english: In the end,
for the one who says [the reason is] weakening the מצוה
it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out the limit of רב פפא's answer in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The אכחושי מצוה explanation of רב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even with long wicks, the מקדש practice was lighting lamp from lamp, which this reason forbids.

steps.title: The challenge stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that the challenge against the אכחושי מצוה reason has no answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concedes that the problem stands. It does not offer an answer for the 'weakening' reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain 'קשיא' means the question is strong and unanswered, but it is not a full refutation (תיובתא). The אכחושי מצוה view is weakened, and the בזוי מצוה view survives.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty that is left unresolved (weaker than a תיובתא)

steps.whatToRemember: After רב ששת's challenge and רב פפא's long-wick answer, the בזוי מצוה reason for רב survives. The אכחושי מצוה reason is left with an unanswered קשיא.

phrases.english: — It is indeed difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that the challenge in step 9 has no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The אכחושי מצוה explanation remains difficult, with no answer given.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the practical conclusion is about lighting from lamp to lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: After all the back-and-forth, the גמרא asks for the bottom line. This sets up the ruling that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Several challenges were raised and answered, some only partly. The גמרא now wants a practical ruling on whether one may light one חנוכה lamp from another.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the conclusion about it?

phrases.english: What is [the conclusion] about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from debate to asking for a practical ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical halacha about lighting from lamp to lamp

steps.title: רב הונא: it depends on whether lighting or placing is the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rules as follows. If the lighting (הדלקה) is the main act of the מצוה, one may light from lamp to lamp. If the placing (הנחה) is the main act, one may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא the son of רב יהושע said: We see. If lighting makes the מצוה, one may light from lamp to lamp. If placing makes the מצוה, one may not light from lamp to lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the bottom line. He ties the question to another open question (an איבעיא) about what the essential act of נר חנוכה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lighting itself is the מצוה, then lighting from another lamp is part of doing the מצוה, and nothing is disrespected. If placing the lamp in its proper spot is the מצוה, then the lighting is only a preparation. Using one מצוה lamp for that preparation would be disrespectful, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: We see / we look at (the deciding factor)
The lighting is what fulfills the מצוה
The placing is what fulfills the מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: The rule for lighting from lamp to lamp depends on the basic definition of נר חנוכה. If הדלקה עושה מצוה, it is permitted. If הנחה עושה מצוה, it is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links a practical question to a basic question about the מצוה itself: is the main act the lighting or the placing? Later פוסקים use that question for many חנוכה laws.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
We see:
if lighting makes the מצוה —
one may light from lamp to lamp.
And if placing makes the מצוה —
one may not light from lamp to lamp.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: חָזֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 with a conditional ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Lighting from lamp to lamp is permitted if הדלקה עושה מצוה, and forbidden if הנחה עושה מצוה.

steps.title: The open question: lighting or placing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presents the question behind רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's ruling. For נר חנוכה, which act fulfills the מצוה: the lighting or the placing?
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Sages asked: Does the lighting do the מצוה, or does the placing do the מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in the full question that Step 12's ruling depended on. It asks which single act of the נר חנוכה is the actual מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate moments: lighting the flame and setting the lamp in its proper spot. If הדלקה is the מצוה, the lighting itself must be done properly. If הנחה is the מצוה, the lighting is only a preparation, and what counts is putting the lit lamp in place.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them (an open question raised among the Sages)
Accomplishes (is the act that fulfills) the מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: This question decides many practical cases, such as lighting in one place and moving the lamp, or holding the lamp in your hand. It also decided the ruling about lighting from lamp to lamp in Step 12.

phrases.english: As it was asked of them (the Sages):
Does lighting accomplish the מצוה,
or does placing accomplish the מצוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the full question that the ruling in Step 12 depended on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which act fulfills the מצוה of נר חנוכה: הדלקה or הנחה?

steps.title: First proof: holding the lamp does not count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from רבא that הנחה is the מצוה. רבא says that someone standing and holding a lit נר חנוכה has done nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as רבא said: If someone was holding a נר חנוכה while standing, he did nothing at all. Conclude from this that placing does the מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a proof. If merely holding the lit lamp does not count, the lamp apparently has to be set down, so placing must be the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lamp in this case is already properly lit, yet the person has still not fulfilled the מצוה. The only thing missing seems to be putting the lamp down. That suggests הנחה is the essential act.

keyTerms.meaning: He did nothing at all (did not fulfill the מצוה)

phrases.english: Come and hear, as Rava said:
If one was holding a Hanukkah lamp and standing —
he did nothing at all.
Conclude from this: placing accomplishes the מצוה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That הנחה is the act that fulfills the מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא: someone holding a lit נר חנוכה while standing has done nothing.

steps.title: Pushing off the first proof: onlookers will misread it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Holding the lamp fails for a different reason: people will think he is holding it for his own use.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the reason is that someone who sees him will say he is holding it for his own needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different reason for רבא's ruling. That reason has nothing to do with whether placing is the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if הדלקה is the מצוה, holding the lamp is a problem. A lamp in someone's hand looks like he is using it for light, not doing a מצוה, so the public message of the נר חנוכה is lost. רבא's ruling is therefore explained without deciding the question.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean placing is unimportant. It only means רבא's case cannot prove that placing is the essential act, because there is another reason the person failed.

phrases.english: There, the one who sees says
he is holding it for his own needs.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The question stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The failure in רבא's case is explained by the onlooker's impression, not by a missing הנחה.

steps.title: Second proof: lighting inside and carrying it out does not count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a second statement of רבא, this time as proof that הדלקה is the מצוה. Lighting inside and then bringing the lamp out does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as רבא said: If he lit it inside and then took it out, he did nothing. It makes sense if lighting does the מצוה: the lighting must be done in its proper place, so he did nothing. But if placing does the מצוה, why did he do nothing? He did place it in the right spot!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a proof in the other direction. Since lighting in the wrong place and then moving the lamp to the right place does not work, the lighting must be the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the placing at the doorway was done correctly, and only the lighting was in the wrong spot. If הנחה were the מצוה, the person should have fulfilled it. Since he did not, it seems הדלקה must happen in the proper place.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine if you say (one side fits; the other side is hard)

phrases.english: Come and hear, as Rava said:
If he lit it inside and took it out —
he did nothing.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא הַדְלָקָה עוֹשָׂה מִצְוָה —
phrases.english: Granted, if you say lighting accomplishes the מצוה —
we require lighting in its proper place,
and that is why he did nothing.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ הַנָּחָה עוֹשָׂה מִצְוָה,
phrases.english: But if you say placing accomplishes the מצוה,
why did he do nothing at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא הַדְלָקָה עוֹשָׂה מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof (for הנחה) failed, this tries a proof for the opposite side.
steps.raayaObject: That הדלקה is the act that fulfills the מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא: someone who lit inside and carried the lamp out has done nothing.

steps.title: Pushing off the second proof: the same onlooker problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this proof with the same idea. Someone who sees him light inside will think he lit it for his own use.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, someone who sees him will say that he lit it for his own needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבא's second ruling with the onlooker reason again. So this case also proves nothing about הדלקה versus הנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lamp lit inside the house looks like ordinary household light. Carrying it outside afterward does not fix how the lighting looked when it happened. The failure therefore does not prove that הדלקה is the essential act.
steps.whatToRemember: Both of רבא's cases, holding the lamp and lighting inside, are explained by one idea: an onlooker would think the light is for personal use. So neither case settles whether הדלקה or הנחה is the מצוה.

phrases.english: There too: the one who sees says
he lit it for his own needs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 16, using the same reasoning as Step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The question stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The failure is explained by the onlooker's impression, not by the lighting being the essential act.

steps.title: Opening a third proof from רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a third attempt to answer the question, quoting רבי יהושע בן לוי. His actual statement comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as רבי יהושע בן לוי said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא is introducing a third proof, and the words of רבי יהושע בן לוי follow right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both proofs from רבא were pushed off, so the question is still open. The גמרא now turns to a different authority, hoping his statement will settle it.

keyTerms.meaning: An early אמורא of ארץ ישראל

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Come and hear, as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
phrases.notes: His statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both proofs from רבא are pushed off, the גמרא introduces a new proof.
steps.raayaObject: To settle whether הדלקה or הנחה fulfills the מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי (continued on the next amud).
